title: Land or retire the unowned untracked preview-goal-landing test that executes in every full-suite gate
description:
apps/daemon/src/preview/preview-goal-landing.test.ts has been sitting UNTRACKED in the shared checkout since 2026-09-05 23:18 local. It is the only untracked test file under apps/daemon: `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- apps/daemon | grep '\.test\.ts$'` returns exactly that one path.

It is not lost work and it is not dirt, which is why it has survived five days and several fleet turnovers without anyone being willing to touch it:

- Its production module IS landed. `apps/daemon/src/preview/preview-goal-landing.ts` and its .js bridge are both tracked, so this is a test for shipped code that was never committed.
- It is GREEN and it EXECUTES. worker-26a27e7c measured it in the 18:46Z Gate 3 full-suite leg and corrected its own GATE END to say so: the daemon leg's 610 -> 611 file count is this file, not the row's new arm. Every gate run silently includes it, so every count line quoted from this host is one file higher than the tracked tree would give.
- Ownership was investigated and NOT established. governor-608c8a78 determined at 11:07Z that it is unowned peer WIP and specifically NOT task-f7d38f752b's delivery, per that row's own comment-550e75fe. No live row claims it. Two governors have now declined to declare_files it on a lineage guess, and declined to delete an untracked file they did not author.

Its two arms assert readGoalLandingStatus: the full `{ allLanded, missing, nodes }` shape for a scoped landing, and that a bare legacy landing cannot approve a scoped preview. Four tracked test files reference readGoalLandingStatus (preview-auto-decision.test.ts, preview-daemon-edge.test.ts, preview-runner.test.ts, and the production preview-daemon-edge.ts), but a read of those shows them using it as a helper assertion on `.allLanded` only. The full-shape arm and the legacy-landing refusal look unique to this file; confirm that rather than trusting this summary.

Commissioned by governor-bd76ac8c on the human's explicit instruction (2026-09-10, "file a small row to land it"), chosen over deleting it or leaving it. Filed rather than governor-landed because hand-landing a source nobody claims is exactly the move that broke HEAD for two hours on 2026-09-06.

Both outcomes are acceptable deliveries. If the coverage is unique, commit it. If it is genuinely duplicated by tracked tests, delete it and say which tracked arms cover each of its two assertions. What is NOT acceptable is leaving it untracked, or committing it without checking for duplication.
definitionOfDone: Duplication is decided on read evidence, not assumed: for EACH of the file's two arms (the full {allLanded, missing, nodes} shape, and the refusal of a bare legacy landing for a scoped preview), name either the tracked test file and arm that already asserts it, or state that none does. Quote the grep or read used.

`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- apps/daemon | grep '\.test\.ts$'` returns EMPTY, reached either by committing the file or by deleting it per the duplication finding. Do not silence it by adding an ignore entry.

`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` EXIT 0 with the `Test Files N passed (N)` count line quoted, taken under full-suite-gate. State the file count and whether it moved: committing the file leaves 611 unchanged because it was already executing untracked, while deleting it drops the count by one. A count that moves the other way means something else changed and must be explained.

No production source under apps/daemon/src/preview is modified. This row lands or retires a test; if the test turns out to be red or to need a production fix to pass, stop and report rather than editing the module.

implementationPlan.description:
PRE-FLIGHT CENSUS AND AN OUT-OF-TREE BACKUP. No edits in this step.

(a) `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/preview` - expect exactly one line, `?? apps/daemon/src/preview/preview-goal-landing.test.ts`. Anything else means a peer is mid-flight in this directory: record it and continue, never revert or stash it.

(b) BACK IT UP BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE. This is untracked peer WIP with no undo until it is staged. Copy it to `%TEMP%\moe-task-36794cfc-preview-goal-landing.test.ts` - the path MUST carry the TASK id, not only your worker id, because seat ids are reused across wrapper relaunches and a seat-keyed temp path on this host has already been found holding a stale vintage. Then record the SHA256 of the LIVE file (not the backup) in the step note; step 6 compares against it.

(c) Record both counts: `git ls-files -- apps/daemon | grep -c '.test.ts$'` (610 at plan time) and the working-tree total tracked+untracked (611 at plan time). These are the numbers step 5 reconciles the gate's file count against.

(d) Note the peer dirt elsewhere in the tree (several modified .moe paths, two untracked .moe/resources files, one untracked markdown at repo root) and leave every one of them alone. Forbidden for the whole task: `git add -A`, `git stash`, `git checkout --`, `git restore`, and `git commit`.

DECIDE DUPLICATION PER ARM, ON READ EVIDENCE. This is DoD clause 1 and it is the step that chooses the delivery.

Run `git grep -n readGoalLandingStatus -- 'apps/**'` - scope the pathspec, a bare git grep drowns in .moe/messages chatter. Then READ each tracked call site in context, not just the matched line.

The file's two arms:
  ARM A - `toEqual({ allLanded: true, missing: [], nodes: ["node-a"] })` after a landing seeded on the SCOPED execution ref.
  ARM B - `toEqual({ allLanded: false, missing: ["node-a"], nodes: ["node-a"] })` after a landing seeded on the BARE node key.

My plan-time read, to VERIFY rather than trust: ARM A IS covered, by preview-runner.test.ts's arm "PASSES the gate once every node of the goal carries a COMMITTED landing" (~:142-152), which lands through its own `land()`/`scopedRef()` helpers (~:57-70, same compiledExecutionRef keying) and asserts `.nodes`, `.missing` and `.allLanded` as three separate expectations - the same three fields. ARM B is NOT covered anywhere: preview-runner.test.ts:124 asserts `.missing` under a REFUSED outcome on a scoped ref (different cause); preview-runner.test.ts:139 lands a SIBLING node `node-1` (the goal-scope concern); preview-daemon-edge.test.ts:292 has no landing at all; preview-daemon-edge.test.ts:76 and preview-auto-decision.test.ts:181 are positive fixture guards inside `landedWorld()`. Nothing tracked seeds a landing under the bare key, which is exactly the legacyCompiledNodeKeys/compiledExecutionRef scoping in `goalNodes`.

BECAUSE ARM B IS UNIQUE, THE DELIVERY IS COMMIT. If your own read contradicts mine, your read wins: if BOTH arms turn out covered by tracked arms, delete the file in step 4 instead of staging it, and name the covering file and arm title for each.

Record the decision as a two-row table (arm -> covering tracked file and arm title, or "none") in a moe.add_comment on this row, quoting the grep you ran. That comment is DoD clause 1's evidence.

RE-MEASURE GREEN, SCOPED, BEFORE ADOPTING THE BYTES. The "it is green" claim in the description is five days old.

Exact command - do NOT use `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test -- <path>`, the literal `--` reaches vitest as match-everything and silently runs the whole suite at exit 0:

  pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json --testTimeout=30000 src/preview/preview-goal-landing.test.ts

Require BOTH count lines: `Test Files 1 passed (1)` and `Tests 2 passed (2)`. Exit 0 with no count line means nothing ran and is not a pass. If you pipe the output, capture ${PIPESTATUS[0]}, not the pipeline's status. Measured at plan time 2026-09-10 21:53 local: exactly those two lines, exit 0.

Do NOT run a mutation drill on this file or on preview-goal-landing.ts. The DoD does not ask for one, the arms already assert whole-object literals rather than truthiness, and an on-disk drill under apps/daemon/src cannot be contained even by a held full-suite gate.

IF IT IS RED: stop. DoD clause 4 forbids touching apps/daemon/src/preview production source, so a red here is not fixable inside this row - call moe.report_blocked with the failing arm quoted.

ADOPT THE PATH: STAGE IT AND DECLARE IT. No hand commit.

(a) `git add -- apps/daemon/src/preview/preview-goal-landing.test.ts` - that exact pathspec and nothing else. Staging is what makes DoD clause 2 satisfiable in-session, because `git ls-files --others` lists only paths absent from the index.

(b) `moe.declare_files` with that one path. You did not author this file, so the wrapper's tool-write harvest will not see it; declare_files is the only thing that puts it into the completion commit's explicit pathspec. Name it in complete_step.modifiedFiles as well.

(c) COMMIT IT VERBATIM. Do not reformat, do not add a header docblock to match the sibling preview tests, do not delete the duplicated Arm A. Any edit to these bytes invalidates the "already green, already executing, the 611 already includes it" measurement the whole row rests on. Prove it: SHA256 of the file now must equal step 1's SHA256, in a call separate from the `git add`.

(d) Verify DoD clause 2: `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- apps/daemon | grep '.test.ts$'` returns EMPTY - grep exits 1 on no match, and that exit 1 is the pass. Quote the command and its empty output. Do NOT reach empty by adding a .gitignore entry; the DoD forbids silencing it.

(e) Forbidden: `git commit`, `git add -A`, `git add` of any other path.

If step 2 concluded BOTH arms are duplicated, this step deletes the file instead: `git rm --cached` does not apply to an untracked path, so simply delete it from disk, note the deletion, and expect the step 5 file count to DROP by one.

THE FULL DAEMON LEG, UNDER THE SHARED GATE. This is DoD clause 3 and the task's named verification command.

(a) `moe.acquire_resource full-suite-gate`. At plan time it is HELD by qa-c85c997d for task-24b68b05, acquired 2026-09-10T18:52:09Z with a 24h expiry, so expect a wait. If refused: say so in chat, then `moe.report_blocked` with `resourceId: "full-suite-gate"` - that keeps your seat and auto-unblocks on grant. Do NOT run the full leg beside a peer's held gate.

(b) With the lease held: post GATE START, run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, post GATE END, release the resource. Quote the `Test Files N passed (N)` line verbatim and the exit code. No count line means nothing ran, whatever the exit code says.

(c) THE FILE COUNT. Expected N = 611 and UNCHANGED, and the record must say WHY: this row stages a file that was already on disk and already collected, so zero bytes moved and vitest collects exactly the same set before and after. Take the PRINTED number as authoritative rather than the DoD's literal 611 - the epic rail forbids trusting a frozen roster count. If N differs, reconcile it in the same window with `git ls-files -- apps/daemon | grep -c '.test.ts$'` (610 at plan time, so 610 + this file = 611) and `git log --since=2026-09-05 --diff-filter=AD --name-only -- 'apps/daemon/**/*.test.ts'` to name the peer rows that added or removed test files. Explain any move; never restate 611 as a fact you did not measure.

(d) IF EXIT 1: apply the epic's path-attributed-baseline rail rather than fabricating green. This row's owned-path set is one file whose bytes are unchanged, so the HEAD-failures-minus-merge-base-failures set intersected with owned paths is empty by construction - state that argument explicitly. Disclose the foreign red verbatim with its exact failing lines and file paths. Note: the 8 reds recorded earlier today in monitoring/health-probe-schedule.test.ts and daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts are GONE at this HEAD (re-measured at plan time: 2 files, 48 tests, exit 0), so do not pre-attribute a red to them.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, THEN THE COMPLETION RECORD.

Run the checklist and record each answer:
  - DoD 4: `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src` shows no modification anywhere under src/preview except the staged add. Zero production source touched.
  - The delivered bytes are the peer's bytes: SHA256 still equals step 1's.
  - Re-run the DoD 2 census. A peer may have dropped a NEW untracked test in the meantime - if so, report it and do NOT adopt it; it is not yours, and the clause is scoped to the file this row was commissioned for.
  - Peer dirty paths from step 1(d) are all still untouched.
  - The %TEMP% backup is stale now and lives out of tree; leave it.

Ask the hostile questions: what if two sessions raced this one file - would my census still be honest? What if the gate ran while a peer was mid-write under apps/daemon? What would I have concluded if the leg printed exit 0 with no count line?

Then write the row comment carrying (1) the per-arm duplication table from step 2, (2) both gate rows as command / exit code / count line, (3) the file-count reasoning. Comments truncate SILENTLY at 5000 chars - keep it under ~4500 and put one idea per comment if it runs long. Only then call moe.complete_task, with `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` as verification.command and its FRESH output tail, and a completionSummary that states plainly which of the two arms was unique and that no bytes on disk changed.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
DELETE THE FILE - rejected on evidence, not preference. Arm B has no tracked counterpart (see insight 4), so deleting it would silently retire the only guard on the bare-key/scoped-ref distinction in `goalNodes`. Kept as the explicit fallback in step 2 in case the worker's own read contradicts mine: if BOTH arms turn out covered, the file is deleted and each covering arm named.

DELETE ONLY THE DUPLICATED ARM A AND COMMIT ARM B - rejected. It edits a peer's bytes for a marginal gain, and Arm A's whole-object `toEqual` is strictly stronger than preview-runner's three field assertions (it also pins the absence of extra keys). The DoD frames the decision at FILE level, and the delivery-bias rail says take the smallest working slice. Commit verbatim.

ADDING A HEADER DOCBLOCK to match the house style of the sibling preview tests - rejected for the same reason. Any edit invalidates the 'already green, already executing, count already includes it' measurement the whole row rests on.

GOVERNOR HAND-LANDING instead of a row - already rejected upstream by the commissioning governor; hand-landing an unclaimed source is what broke HEAD for two hours on 2026-09-06.

A MUTATION DRILL to prove the two arms non-vacuous - deliberately NOT planned. The DoD does not ask for it; the arms already assert whole-object literals rather than truthiness, which is the repo's own non-vacuity bar; and an on-disk drill under apps/daemon/src cannot be contained even by a held full-suite gate (module-load reads happen on unleased daemon spawns).

planningNotes.risks:
UNTRACKED PEER FILE HAS NO UNDO until it is staged. A stray `git add -A`, `git stash`, `git checkout --` or `git restore` destroys five days of surviving work with no recovery. Back it up out of tree FIRST, keyed by TASK id (seat ids are reused across wrapper relaunches and a seat-keyed %TEMP% path has already held a stale vintage on this host).

THE DoD's 611 IS A FROZEN ROSTER COUNT and the epic rail forbids trusting one. Take the PRINTED count as authoritative and reconcile it against `git ls-files -- apps/daemon | grep -c '\.test\.ts$'` measured in the same window, not against the literal.

AN EXIT-0 LEG WITH NO COUNT LINE RAN NOTHING. `Test Files N passed (N)` is the discriminator. Also: a piped run reports tail's status - capture ${PIPESTATUS[0]}.

THE FULL-SUITE GATE IS PEER-HELD with a 24h lease. Do not run the full daemon leg beside it. The sanctioned wait is report_blocked with resourceId - it keeps the seat and auto-unblocks on grant.

DoD 4 IS A HARD FENCE. If the file turns out red, or would need a change in apps/daemon/src/preview to pass, stop and report. Do not edit the production module.

STAGING vs COMMITTING. The worker never authored this file, so the wrapper's tool-write harvest will not see it; moe.declare_files is the only thing that puts it in the completion commit's pathspec. `git add -- <exact path>` is what makes the DoD 2 census pass in-session, since `--others` lists only paths absent from the index. Both are needed. Never hand-run `git commit`.

A RACE ON THE SAME FILE. If a peer session stages or deletes it first, the census answers EMPTY without this row doing anything - say so honestly rather than claiming the adoption.
